synthesis: Nine retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Before-after and stepped studies suggest that structured templates and coordinators raise documentation completeness by roughly 20 to 30 percentage points, with a within-board intraclass correlation of about 0.12, and that monthly feedback sustains the gain. Incomplete documentation is linked to later first treatment, though confounded by case complexity. Meetings lengthen briefly after adoption. A validated five-item questionnaire measures patients' understanding in about 4 minutes. Methods work shows that with about a dozen clusters a stepped-wedge design has far more power than a parallel cluster design, provided secular trends are modelled.
gradeRationale: No randomised evaluation of templates; consistent before-after and stepped observational evidence at risk of bias; methods and measurement evidence is stronger but indirect.
summary: Nine retrieved records appraised; six claims; overall certainty low.
